newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - AVI year profit seen edging up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - AVI year profit seen edging up.

text.p: Profits are only expected to edge up at South Africa's Anglovaal Industries Ltd (AVI) when it posts year figures on Wednesday as its wide spread of businesses continue to encounter patchy markets, analysts said Friday.

Analysts forecast pre-exceptional earnings per share to come in on a range of 159.7 cents to 170.0, compared to 155.6 last time. The dividend was seen being hiked to 29-31 cents a share from 28 cents.
One analyst said the market consensus for the firm was for earnings per share of 164 cents and a dividend payout of 30 cents.

Holding firm AVI has a broad range of interests including packaging and rubber firm Consol, its AVI Diversified engineering and textiles arm, construction and electronics firm Grinaker Holdings and foods group Irvin & Johnson.
Analysts said trading across the group had been mixed with Irvin & Johnson underperforming while Consol had traded well.
During the first half of the year AVI's margins tightened slightly as conditions in consumer markets toughened, imports rose and there was an increase in competition from international rivals.
But analysts said margins were unlikely to have been squeezed too much further in the second half.

"There will still be pressure, but I don't think they will come down much more," said one analyst who declined to be named. The analyst said she had downgraded profit estimates for the firm recently due to the patchy underlying markets.
